summary.headline: IIFL Capital Q2 FY27 consolidated operational revenue rose 14% QoQ to INR722 crores, but a INR32 crore BSE mark-to-market loss left reported profit weaker.
summary.overview: Consolidated operational revenue was INR722 crores, up 14% QoQ and 22% YoY, with retail equities at INR316 crores (up 6% QoQ) and institutional and banking revenue at INR245 crores (up 18% QoQ). Operational PBT before mark-to-market was INR206 crores, up about 40% QoQ, but an adverse BSE share price move produced a INR32 crore MTM loss. Costs rose on employee expenses (INR194 crores, up 26% YoY), finance costs (INR75 crores, up 25% QoQ) and admin/technology spend. Corporate events included the Fairfax preferential infusion and open offer, expected to close in November 2026 with Fairfax taking 51%, a proposed wholly owned NBFC subsidiary for HNI lending, and the appointment of Vasudev Jagannath as Whole-Time Director, to be designated MD from 1 January 2027.

segments.name: Retail equities
segments.commentary: Income of INR316 crores in Q2 FY27, up 6% QoQ and about 17% YoY; H1 at INR613 crores, up 15% YoY.

segments.name: Institutional and banking
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR245 crores, up 18% QoQ and 31% YoY. Management split the approximately INR450 crore combined institutional broking and investment banking revenue as about INR250 crores broking and about INR200 crores institutional investment banking.

segments.name: FPD (distribution)
segments.commentary: Income of INR159 crores, up 27% QoQ and about 23% YoY. Insurance income underperformed in Q2; growth came from ARR income on AIF, PMS and mutual funds. Wealth business is still loss-making.

segments.name: Wealth / AMC
segments.commentary: Wealth RM net additions were marginal in Q2. PMS AUM declined on NDPMS outflows, which management expects to recover. Wealth break-even expected in 6 to 18 months; in-house manufacturing of about INR4,500 crores is ongoing and will take longer to break even.

guidance_outlook: Employee cost to run at about INR192-194 crores per quarter going forward, per management's confirmation of the run-rate.
Fairfax preferential allotment and open offer expected to close in November 2026; Fairfax to join the promoter group with 51% stake.
Wealth/FPD business expected to break even in 6 to 18 months; in-house manufacturing will extend that timeline.
Insurance income expected to show some uptick over the next two quarters; long-term focus shifts to capital markets distribution over insurance.
Proposed wholly owned NBFC subsidiary for HNI lending and credit solutions, subject to RBI approval.
Vasudev Jagannath to be designated Managing Director effective 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approvals; R. Venkataraman remains on the Board.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing (wealth/product) of roughly INR4,500 crores under way, with ongoing investment; break-even will take longer.
Branch and technology investments drove depreciation up 16% YoY and admin expense up 11% YoY, mainly on tech.
Wealth RM headcount broadly flat in Q2; AMC business added some headcount (about 5% overall headcount increase YoY).
Finance costs up 40% YoY on higher borrowings, with growth in the MTM book cited as a driver.
demand_pricing: ADTO of INR3,05,073 crores in Q2 FY27 was down about 3% QoQ, outperforming the wider market volume decline per management; up 16% YoY.
Typical fee on in-house equity products about 2-2.5%, while third-party products earn roughly half that (about 1-1.25%); management described these as rough figures.
RBI regulations effective Q2 had only marginal impact on broking, as the company has no proprietary trading book.
PMS AUM declined in Q2 on NDPMS outflows; management expects recovery in coming days.

qa_highlights.question: How many RMs were added and what is the split between institutional broking and investment banking revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Net RM additions were marginal (single digits at most). Combined institutional broking and IB revenue was about INR450 crores: roughly INR250 crores broking and about INR200 crores institutional investment banking.

qa_highlights.question: How will Fairfax funds be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Bulk of the funds will go to margin funding book growth and repayment of borrowings. Management will share exact details from the open offer document by email.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the PMS AUM decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Outflows in NDPMS drove the decline; management hopes to recover them in the coming days.

qa_highlights.question: What drives FPD income going forward, and what is the insurance outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth in ARR AUM is the key driver; insurance income should see some uptick in the next two quarters. Insurance has become marginal and the long-term focus is capital markets distribution. Management is open to selling insurance business if it enhances shareholder value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RBI regulation impact on broking and the employee cost run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact on broking was marginal because there is no prop book. Management confirmed about INR194 crores per quarter for employee cost, citing headcount (about 5% YoY), variable pay and wage inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the open offer structure and will promoters tender?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters and promoter group will not tender in the open offer. If the offer does not take Fairfax to 51%, promoters will sell shares to get there.

risks_watch: BSE share MTM volatility: the 5.95 lakh BSE shares drove a INR32 crore loss in Q2 after a gain in Q1, so other income remains price-dependent.
Finance cost up 40% YoY on rising borrowings; funds from Fairfax are partly earmarked for repaying borrowings.
Wealth/FPD business still loss-making; break-even timeline (6-18 months) is uncertain given INR4,500 crore in-house manufacturing investment. Loss quantum not disclosed.
Insurance distribution income underperforming; possible divestment under consideration.
Fairfax open offer closing and the 51% stake transfer, plus the planned NBFC subsidiary, depend on regulatory approvals.
Management did not disclose the UHNI share of FPD AUM or the H1 wealth loss; follow-up by email/call promised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum in broking and banking, with clear optimism on the Fairfax closing. Cautious on macro (geopolitics, oil, rates) and on wealth/FPD profitability. Several questions on the wealth loss, UHNI AUM and Fairfax deployment were deferred to follow-up communication.
key_quotes: India remains resilient. Our GDP is showing signs of growth.
We have seen traction in broking as well as banking.
this entire insurance business has become marginal.
we will focus more on the capital markets distribution rather than insurance distribution.

growth.why: No revenue growth guidance given; management confirmed only an employee cost run-rate of INR192-194 crore per quarter, and the wealth/FPD break-even is 6-18 months out with no capacity or order backing, while in-house manufacturing (~INR4,500 crore) is ongoing without a stated live date.

mgmt.note: Vasudev Jagannath appointed Whole-Time Director, to be designated MD effective 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approvals; no growth plan with targets stated in the brief.
initiatives: Proposed wholly owned NBFC subsidiary for HNI lending and credit solutions, subject to RBI approval

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operational PBT before MTM rose about 40% QoQ to INR206 crores, but employee cost is guided flat at INR192-194 crores per quarter and finance cost is up 25% QoQ, so margin gains depend on revenue staying up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No broking or branch capacity addition was guided; the only build is in-house wealth manufacturing (about INR4,500 crores) with no live date, and tech/branch spend lifted depreciation 16% YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: ADTO was INR3,05,073 crores, down about 3% QoQ but up 16% YoY, and PMS AUM fell on NDPMS outflows that management expects to recover; RM net additions were marginal.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was disclosed and no new capex plan was announced beyond the ongoing INR4,500 crore in-house manufacturing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was given; only an employee cost run-rate of INR192-194 crores per quarter was confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Finance cost is up 40% YoY and 25% QoQ, the BSE MTM swung to a INR32 crore loss, and wealth/FPD is still loss-making with break-even 6-18 months out.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The proposed wholly owned NBFC subsidiary for HNI lending is subject to RBI approval, and no product launch date was given.

rows.label: Fairfax 51% stake and open offer close
rows.why: Expected to close in November 2026 with Fairfax taking 51%, and promoters will sell shares if the offer falls short; funds mainly go to margin book growth and repaying borrowings.

rows.label: Fairfax funds used to repay borrowings
rows.why: Finance cost rose 40% YoY to INR75 crores in Q2 and part of the Fairfax infusion is earmarked to repay borrowings, which could ease the interest drag.

rows.label: Wealth/FPD break-even
rows.why: Management guides 6-18 months to break-even, but the INR4,500 crore in-house manufacturing will extend that and the loss is undisclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on broking and banking momentum and the Fairfax closing, but cautious on macro and wealth/FPD profitability; analysts pressed on the wealth loss, UHNI AUM and Fairfax deployment, which were deferred to follow-up.
